clue.text: Naval escort provided by company?

definitions.meaning: split in two, a vessel that sails alongside and accompanies another
the state of being with others, fellowship

explanation.surface: A question about whether a warship's escort is laid on by some firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words and it is a ship that keeps another company; as one word it is company itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel acting as a companion is a naval escort, and fellowship with others is what company means.

clue.text: Removed obstructions and was acquitted

definitions.meaning: took away what was blocking, as a path or drain

explanation.surface: Someone who unblocked something and was then found innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: To unblock is to take away the obstructions, and a defendant found not guilty has had their name freed of the charge.

clue.text: Drove Tom round and round, Rosy followed

indicators.note: says the next piece comes after the others
turning a name round means reading it from the end back

parts.note: taken as written
a round shape like a ring is the letter O
rosy means red

explanation.surface: A driver took Tom round and round in circles, and someone called Rosy came after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' appears twice with two different jobs: the first is the reversal signal, the second is the ring-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have motored is to have travelled by car, which is driving.

clue.text: Some boil I accepted was connected with the intestines

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A patient's boil was linked to a gut complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Iliac is the anatomical adjective for the ileum or ilium region, the lower small intestine and hip area.

clue.text: Algernon stopped piece that had not been interrupted

indicators.note: a piece is only part of the words before it, so the letters are found within them

explanation.surface: Algernon halted a performance that had been running continuously.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of 'Algernon' and the start of 'stopped'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonstop runs without pause, never broken off.

clue.text: Harry cares about rock-rabbits, dassies etc

annotationWithheld.why: Harry cares about rock-rabbits, dassies etc (7): the printed fodder HARRY CARES has ten letters and cannot give the seven of the answer; no parse uses every word, so a word is misprinted or missing
annotationWithheld.clue: Harry cares about rock-rabbits, dassies etc

clue.text: Eaten behind a screen?

parts.note: food that has been eaten has disappeared, just as something placed behind a screen is hidden from view

explanation.surface: A diner secretly eating behind a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden from view describes both a meal consumed and an object concealed by a screen.

clue.text: Noise of a turn-table?

indicators.note: a turn here means a change of order, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what sound a record turntable makes.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes 'turn-table' look like a record deck; split it and 'turn' tells you to rearrange 'table'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleat is the cry of a sheep or goat, a kind of noise.

clue.text: Two drinks made very quickly

definitions.meaning: a brace is a pair, and shakes are milkshakes
in no time at all, as in the idiom 'in a couple of shakes'

explanation.surface: A pair of beverages whipped up in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace means a pair, so two milkshakes; the idiom 'in a brace of shakes' means in an instant.

clue.text: Top half of school used by a spider!

parts.note: a spinning top is a spinner

indicators.note: only the front half of the school's name is used

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Spiders occupying the upper floor of a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top half' looks like the upper part of a building; 'Top' is the toy and 'half of' cuts ETON to its front half. ETON is an elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinneret is the organ a spider spins silk from, so it is what the spider uses for its web.

clue.text: Highly vocal women

parts.note: not loud talkers but singers whose voices sit at the top of the range

explanation.surface: Women who are very outspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female singing voice belongs to these singers, given here in the Italian plural.

clue.text: Breeze to subside during landing of supplies

parts.note: a light breeze is air
to subside is to drop

explanation.surface: The wind easing off while supplies are being delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies dropped by parachute from an aircraft arrive by this means of delivery.

clue.text: Teach another copper going round about a resinous substance

indicators.note: the two letters for the metal surround the rest

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: another version of the word, its letters set in a new order

explanation.surface: A second copper teaching about a resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the anagram signal for 'Teach', and 'going round' puts the copper symbol around the result; 'about' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Catechu is an astringent extract from acacia wood, used in tanning and dyeing, treated as a resin.

clue.text: Broke off, having reached a conclusion

explanation.surface: Talks were halted once a decision was reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean finished: a discussion stopped short, and a story that has run to its close.

clue.text: Not in favour of pop, by the way, having no appetiser

parts.note: against, anti
pop is a word for father, pa
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes fizzy drinks and, incidentally, skips starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' wants to be the drink; it is father.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter course, served before the main meal.

clue.text: Eat glue removed from insects' scales

indicators.note: the letters are moved out of their order and set down afresh

explanation.surface: Eating glue taken off an insect's scales.
explanation.definitionFit: Tegulae are the small scale-like plates at the base of an insect's forewings.

clue.text: Shrewd, not suffering from myopia

definitions.meaning: able to see distant things clearly

explanation.surface: Someone sharp who also has good eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight about the future is shrewdness, and literal long sight is the opposite of short sight.

clue.text: Knock sailor up at last repeatedly

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: the last piece is given over and over, here twice

explanation.surface: Someone woke a sailor at last by banging again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like 'finally'; 'at' is fodder and 'last repeatedly' doubles it after RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-a-tat is the sound of repeated rapping on a door.

clue.text: Retired title holders' timer ie to be replaced

definitions.note: the definition carries a possessive; the answer is the plain plural

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a different place, rearranged

explanation.surface: Retired professors' clock must be swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are those, such as professors, who keep an honorary title after retirement.

clue.text: Moans about the reported sticky material

indicators.note: as spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: size is a gluey sizing used on paper or walls

explanation.surface: Grumbles about the gluey stuff mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighs are long breaths of sorrow or weariness, like moans.

clue.text: One type of shirt used as a vest

explanation.surface: A garment that doubles as underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless top, worn by athletes or as an undergarment.

clue.text: My brig's undergoing an overhaul in port

indicators.note: being overhauled means taken apart and rebuilt, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A sailor's two-masted ship is being refitted in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Grimsby is a fishing port on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimsby is a harbour town on the Humber estuary, a fishing port.

clue.text: Out of top gear

parts.note: not about a car's fifth gear, but having no headwear on

explanation.surface: A car that has dropped out of its highest gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is what goes on top, so being without it means being bareheaded.

clue.text: Vulgar language describing new scum on molten metal outside

parts.note: slag is the waste that forms on melted ore

explanation.surface: Coarse words describing the dross on a smelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, often coarse speech outside standard usage.

clue.text: Making cuts in private education here?

definitions.meaning: piercing with a blade, as with a boil
... College is an English private school in West Sussex

explanation.surface: Budget cuts in private schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCING is also the name of a fee-paying school in Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening with a blade is making cuts, and a famous fee-paying school bears this name.

clue.text: Heard cat disturb the bird

indicators.note: a heard word is a spoken one, so these words sound like another

parts.note: a cat is a kitty, and to disturb is to wake

explanation.surface: A cat was heard to upset the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of northern sea cliffs.

clue.text: Composer is last character to be taken in by the officer

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: Lt is a lieutenant
taken as written
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A composer is the last person an officer would be fooled by.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Well-placed to have one's picture taken?

explanation.surface: Someone in a good position sitting for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being comfortably fortunate, and literally it is posing attractively for a photo.
